topic.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Tangent and Cotangent

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\tan{\left(\dfrac{3x}{5}+C\right)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

\begin{align*} y & =\tan{\left( \dfrac {3x} 5+C\right)}\\[5pt] & =\tan{\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\left(x+\dfrac{5C}{3}\right)\right)}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

The factor $x+\dfrac{5C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\left(x+\dfrac{5C}{3}\right)\right)$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3x}{5}\right).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3x}{5}\right)$ by $\dfrac{\pi}{3}-0=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ units to the right. Therefore:

\[ \dfrac{5C}{3}= -\dfrac{\pi}{3} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C = \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C =-\dfrac{\pi}{5} \]

Since $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{5}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\dfrac{\pi}{5}.$

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \tan\left(\dfrac{3x}{2} + C\right),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows: \begin{align*} y & =\tan\left( \dfrac{3x}{2} + C\right)\\[5pt] & = \tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\left(x + \dfrac{2C}{3}\right) \right)\\[5pt] \end{align*}

The factor $x+\dfrac{2C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\left(x+\dfrac{2C}{3}\right)\right)$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}\right).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\tan\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}\right)$ by $\dfrac{\pi}{4}-0=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ units to the right. Therefore

\[ \dfrac{2C}{3} = -\dfrac{\pi}{4} \quad \Longrightarrow\quad C = -\dfrac{3\pi}{8}. \]

Since $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < C < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $-\dfrac{3\pi}{8}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\dfrac{3\pi}{8}.$

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\cot{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B-2D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{5} . \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\cot(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get

\[ \dfrac{\pi}{5}= \dfrac{\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)} =5 . \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $-\dfrac{3}{2}$ unit down. Hence, $D=-\dfrac{3}{2}.$

Therefore, $B-2D= 5- 2\cdot\left(-\dfrac 3 2\right) =5 +3=8.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

\[ y=\cot\left(5x\right)-\dfrac{3}{2} . \]
